Subject: RFI: TAM coverage, RPO/RTO expectations, and escalation matrix

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking our RFI. As part of the vendor evaluation for our cloud inference platform procurement, we need a concise appendix describing your support model. Specifically we need:

- TAM coverage model (hours, geographic support overlap, on-call rotations)
- RTO/RPO commitments for different severity levels and what remediation steps are guaranteed
- Clear escalation matrix (who is contacted at each step, SLAs for callback/escalation)
- Example incident notification timeline (email/SMS/phone and expected times)

Can you attach a short appendix (PDF) and a CSV that maps severity->RTO/RPO for review by our SOC and procurement teams? Ideally by COB PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Amelia Price
Director, Vendor Programs
FinBridge Financial

Subject: Re: RFI: TAM coverage, RPO/RTO expectations, and escalation matrix

Amelia —

Appreciate the clear asks. Please find attached a short appendix and an RTO/RPO mapping CSV that map our standard commitments by severity. Highlights up front:

- TAM coverage: 24x7 coverage via a primary TAM for Business Hours (09:00-17:00 PT) + on-call rotation for critical incidents outside those hours. We provide a named primary TAM and a secondary on-call TAM for all enterprise Dedicated and Private deployments.
- RTO/RPO: For Severity 1 (production down impacting core inference) typical RTO is 2 hours for Dedicated customers (with reserved capacity) and 4 hours for hosted customers with escalation; RPO depends on configured cache/replication (we've included typical values in the CSV).
- Escalation matrix: first-tier TAM -> Support Escalation Engineer -> On-call SRE -> Customer Success Director (if incident > 8 hours) -> CTO on request. Contact methods and expected callback windows are in appendix.

Attachments: RFI_FinBridge_Appendix_TAM_RPO_RTO.pdf; Incident_RTO_RPO_SLA_Table.csv

I'll loop in Neha (CS lead) and Kim (Support Ops) to add operational details and any FinBridge-specific phrasing you need.

Next steps: If this looks plausible, we can convert to your template and add the PR/PO language for the contract.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra

Amelia –

Adding operational detail per your SOC team's needs. A few clarifications and commitments we can make in the RFI appendix:

1) TAM on-call cadence and handoff
- Primary TAM: named resource, covers account management and weekday BAU (09:00–17:00 PT).
- Secondary on-call TAM: rotates weekly across regional TAM pool; 24x7 pager for Severity 1 incidents.
- Handoffs are documented in PagerDuty with 30-minute overlap for scheduled rotations.

2) Incident severity mapping (summary)
- Sev 1: major production impact (customers blocked). RTO target: 2 hours (Dedicated) / 4 hours (Hosted fallback). RPO: best-effort to restore within last 15 minutes for Dedicated with continuous cache replication; Hosted depends on customer configuration.
- Sev 2: partial outage / degraded performance. RTO target: 8 business hours. RPO: up to 1 hour.
- Sev 3: minor issue, next-business-day fix window.

3) Notification channels and cadence
- T+0: automated incident page + email distribution to TAM and Support (within 15 mins of detection)
- T+30m: first callback from TAM/Support triage
- T+2h: SRE escalation summary and remediation ETA (for Sev 1)
- T+8h: executive update (if not resolved) to Customer Success Director and FinBridge stakeholders

4) Evidence & compliance items we can provide on request
- Incident logs (redacted), SOC 2 subservice evidence, audit trail of callbacks, and post-incident RCA within 5 business days for Sev 1.

Kim — can you confirm the on-call rotation details and provide the example PagerDuty runbook link we can include?

Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
